rules_text:
Rules summary Full rules and an animated card guide: isle-of-bears.heybyedesign.com/rules Isle of Bears is a two-player abstract. Summer, 2050 — the Arctic is nearly ice-free, and homeless white bears have climbed aboard the black bears' isle. One isle cannot hold two kinds of bear. Contents 1 Objective 2 Board 3 Turn sequence 4 Card effects 5 Rulings worth knowing 6 Winning 7 On BGA Objective Win the moment every occupied space is topped by bears of your colour . The bear on top of a stack controls that space, and every bear beneath it. Board 4 isles, each 2×2, making a 4×4 grid of 16 spaces. 16 bears start on the board, one per space — 8 white, 8 black. Each player has a deck of 13 action cards and a hand of 3, face up . Both hands are public information; only the deck order is hidden. Turn sequence Play one card, then resolve these steps in order: Play a card — choose one of your three face-up cards and resolve its effect. A card affects all bears on a space; a stack always moves together. Overcrowding — a space safely holds 5 bears. If any space holds 6 or more after the effect resolves, all of the opponent's bears on that space are removed from the game (they fall into the sea). Only the active player's bears stay. Sinking isles — any isle with no bears left on it sinks and is removed from play. Its spaces no longer exist. Discard & draw — the cards used this turn go to their owner's discard pile, then you draw back up to 3. If your deck runs out, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck. Play then passes to your opponent. Card effects Each player has the same 13 cards. See the animated card guide for a before → after board for every card. Straight — Move the whole stack any distance up, down, left or right — landing on other stacks on top. Diagonal — Same idea, but along the four diagonals. Leap — Any direction, any distance — move the stack to any space on the board. Swap — Two spaces trade their entire stacks. Party — The four orthogonal neighbours all pile onto the centre; you choose the stacking order. Push — Your own bear is the pusher and moves along; all eight directions work (an empty direction is a plain one-step move), and a bear pushed off the isle falls into the sea. Dismiss — Released one at a time from the bottom up — each bear goes next to the previous one (restacking allowed), spreading out like a path. Banish — Pick a space: every bear there, including your own, goes into the sea. Play Twice — Activate other cards in front of you, two activations in total — two different cards, or the same one twice. Discard a Card — Send one of your opponent's face-up cards to their discard pile; they draw only at the end of their turn. Wild Card — Activate any face-up card from either player — Play Twice included. On an opponent's card, black and white swap. Everything used is discarded together. Rulings worth knowing "Your bears" is decided by the colour on top of a stack. When Wild Card activates an opponent's card, "your" always means the player who played the Wild Card. Straight and Diagonal may pass over sunken gaps , but must land on a space that still exists. Push : the pushed line stops at the first empty space (bears beyond it are unaffected). The pusher's destination must exist, so directions that would push it off the board are not offered. Dismiss : a bear may be placed back onto a space you already used, and stacks may re-form as you go. Swap needs bears on both spaces. Wild Card may activate Play Twice , but Wild cannot activate another Wild, and Play Twice cannot activate Play Twice or Wild — that would allow infinite chains. A card with no legal target may still be played — the effect fizzles, and the card is discarded as usual. If a player would start their turn with no cards (possible via Wild → opponent's Play Twice → your Discard a Card twice), that turn is skipped and their hand is refilled to 3. Winning The moment every occupied space is topped by the same colour, that player wins immediately. If no bears are left at sea level at all, the game is a draw. Tie-breaker — the number of spaces you control at the end of the game. On BGA Both hands are face up by design — this is not a hidden-information game. If a player quits, a zombie takes over so the table can finish. It plays a random legal move; it is not an AI opponent.

community_text:
[Rating: 7/10] Fun but too luck dependent. The play twice action is too strong and there are very weak cards like swap.

[Rating: 7.5/10] A gorgeous 2-players game with nice production and cute artwork by the designer themselves. The game has many tactic decision with some luck of card draw built into it. But the game is quick and you can always got for another game.

[Rating: 8.25/10] Tutorial & Review: https://youtu.be/fhprPDxd5uI  This title was such a wonderful surprise! Not only is it super cute, but it's also a very tactile game that's surprisingly cutthroat and brutal!  It's another brilliant game from the designer, who also brought us the abstract game PWNED! last year. I would absolutely love to see Isle of Bears receive an international release, as I've found this to be quite an exceptional two player abstract strategy game!

[Rating: 9/10] A small game that strikes a balance between strategy and luck, but the art style is really cute.

[Rating: 10/10] Played this twice and liked it a lot. Easy to teach, quick to play, and the stacking part is really fun. Good for 2 players who want something short but smart.

[Rating: 10/10] An amazing and super-cute game. The components are fantastic, and its a super-nice game to enjoy with your significant other!

[Rating: 10/10] This is another one of those games I liked the moment I saw it — the cuteness of the bears, and the colourful, eye-catching art. I got this game at the convention in Taiwan; it was literally the first game sitting at the front of the event, and one of the games that made me decide to fly over and buy it in Taiwan. In this game you control either the white or the black bears, and it's strictly a 2-player game. Your goal is to do whatever it takes so that only your bears remain.
